supersedes: v2.1 (kept in results/p1-test-02/protocol_used.json). v3 keeps every v2.1 rule and adds the H1 acquisition-policy question.
hypothesis: H1: a fixed acquisition policy that prefers tools with few successes and, within a tool, untried signatures one literal away from a known success ('contrast') yields rules that fix C's sort/backup failures; 'scarce' (tool weighting only) is the ablation.
primary: C strict completion under policy=contrast vs C under policy=novelty (results/p1-test-02), paired by (seed, task); same test split, seeds, budget, 300 steps; computed by `python -m atanor_os compare`
decision: H1 GAIN if C(contrast)-C(novelty) >= min_gain_pp and seeds_ge >= 4; NO GAIN if <= 0; else INCONCLUSIVE. Secondary: same for scarce; C-B inside each run; rule exactness per tool from model_C.json (known from the dev coverage check: contrast gives exact convert rules in 4/5 seeds).
conditions: A, B, C + ORACLE (D omitted: its question was answered in v2 and it costs ~10x)
invalid_if: validity tests not run or failed
known_limits: blocked is structurally 0 (the planner never proposes capability-gated tools)
B is exact-signature retrieval and therefore coverage-limited; C-B mixes rule induction with generalization beyond the explored signatures (docs_share column makes this visible)
md objects already occur during exploration (POOL); what is new in test: object and directory names, 3-4 files, extensions log/json, depth-2 target chains, more required steps
the dev coverage check used the same exploration seeds as the test run, so rule-exactness outcomes were seen before freezing; test-task completion was not
iteration_cap: P2 allows at most 3 single-hypothesis changes (H1 is the first)
